title: Setting Up an International MOU or Agreement
summary: How to get a memorandum of understanding or other agreement with a non-U.S. partner reviewed, approved and signed at Yale.
key_considerations: Agreements or MOUs that set up a relationship with a non-U.S. institution need consultation with both OIA and the Office of General Counsel (OGC).
Get approval from your Dean (or designee) first, ideally before other consultations.
OIA checks whether Yale already has a relationship with the partner.
If the agreement involves sponsored research, the Office of Sponsored Projects (OSP) must also be consulted.
Work with foreign government officials, ministries or agencies also needs the Dean, OIA, OSP and OGC.
Keep written records of every consultation and approval, and start early.

steps.title: Get Dean approval
steps.detail: Ask your cognizant Dean, Director or equivalent to approve the proposed partnership.

steps.title: Consult OIA
steps.detail: Email OIA to find out if Yale already works with this partner.

steps.title: Read the OGC MOU guide
steps.detail: OGC publishes an end-user guide for its International MOU system.

steps.title: Submit an agreement request
steps.detail: Use OGC's Agreement Request Form, linked from the International MOUs page, and track its status there. OGC helps with terms and arranges signature.

steps.title: Bring in OSP if research is funded
steps.detail: If money or sponsored research is involved, contact OSP about the agreement.

resources.title: 7000 PR.01 International Activities: Consultation, Review, and Approval
resources.note: Who must review which international activities

resources.title: World Toolkit: approvals for commitments outside the U.S.

good_to_know: For help with the International MOU system, OGC lists Carolyn Marks (carolyn.marks@yale.edu).
When several offices are involved, the International Operations & Compliance Committee (iocc@yale.edu) can coordinate.
High-risk proposals (IP, data security, national security, human rights) may be referred to the IRPA Committee.

title: Adjunct and Visiting Appointments for Partners (School of Medicine)
summary: How a partner based at another institution can get an adjunct or visiting research faculty appointment at Yale School of Medicine.

office.name: YSM Office of Academic and Professional Development (Faculty Affairs)

key_considerations: Adjunct ranks are for people who mainly hold a position at another institution and collaborate with YSM faculty or programs.
Adjunct terms run up to three years at assistant professor and up to five years at associate professor or professor.
Adjunct faculty cannot be principal dissertation advisers or vote on faculty appointments.
Visiting research faculty appointments are for collaborators who need to be on campus and use Yale labs.
Visiting research faculty need outside salary support (not personal funds) and are not Yale employees or paid from Yale funds.

steps.title: Pick the right appointment
steps.detail: Use an adjunct rank for an ongoing collaborator based elsewhere, or a visiting research appointment for someone coming to work in Yale labs.

steps.title: Work with your department
steps.detail: Talk to your department chair and business office about starting the request.

steps.title: Prepare the visiting application
steps.detail: For visiting research faculty, gather a CV, the Visiting Research Faculty Application, signed attestation, proof of funding and proof of insurance.

steps.title: Get approval before inviting
steps.detail: OAPD must approve a visiting application before a formal invitation goes out. Submit it by email to Faculty Affairs.

steps.title: Plan immigration if needed
steps.detail: If the person needs a visa, the department works with OISS once the appointment is approved.

good_to_know: With chair and dean approval, adjunct faculty may serve as PIs on grants.
Visiting research faculty must be in residence at Yale during the appointment.
Other Yale schools have their own appointment processes; contact your dean's office.

title: Hosting International Visitors at Yale
summary: How to bring an international partner or scholar to Yale, from appointment and J-1 sponsorship to research security checks.
key_considerations: The host department starts the process; the visitor needs an approved academic appointment before OISS sponsorship.
Yale-sponsored J-1 requests are made by the department in MyOISS, and OISS decides the J-1 category.
OISS advises allowing 6 to 8 weeks to issue the visa document, not counting visa appointment waits.
Before hosting visitors tied to a Country of Concern or embargoed country, contact the Research Integrity & Security Office (RISO).
You may need to list a visiting scientist as Other Support to federal sponsors.

steps.title: Secure the appointment
steps.detail: Get the academic appointment approved through the right office (for YSM, Faculty Affairs; for postdocs, the Office of Postdoctoral Affairs).

steps.title: Check research security
steps.detail: If the visitor is affiliated with a Country of Concern or embargoed country, email RISO before the collaboration.

steps.title: Submit the J-1 request
steps.detail: The department completes the J-1 sponsorship request in MyOISS, and the scholar fills in their part.

steps.title: Scholar applies for the visa
steps.detail: After the DS-2019 is issued, the scholar pays the SEVIS fee and applies for the visa.

steps.title: Update sponsor disclosures
steps.detail: Once visit terms are set, check whether the visitor must be reported as Other Support.

resources.title: OISS: Visa Options for Faculty and Researchers

good_to_know: For visits by senior officials or heads of state, the Office of International Affairs can help.
Countries of Concern listed by Yale include China, North Korea, Russia and Iran; the lists can change.
important: Contact research.security@yale.edu before hosting anyone affiliated with a Country of Concern or embargoed country.

title: Checking a Partner Before You Engage
summary: How to screen a foreign partner for sanctions, restricted parties and research security risks before you sign or collaborate.
key_considerations: Yale screens people and organizations it works with against U.S. government restricted party lists.
You may not host visitors, sign contracts or do business with anyone on a U.S. restricted party list.
Partners tied to a Country of Concern or embargoed country need a RISO review before collaboration.
OIA can tell you whether Yale already has a relationship with the partner.
Paying a supplier abroad out of pocket still requires screening first.

steps.title: Check existing ties
steps.detail: Email OIA at world@yale.edu to see if Yale already works with this partner.

steps.title: Request restricted party screening
steps.detail: Ask the Export Controls Office to screen the partner organization and key people.

steps.title: Check country risk
steps.detail: If the partner is in or linked to a Country of Concern or embargoed country, contact RISO.

steps.title: Plan disclosures
steps.detail: Once terms are set, check what you must disclose to Yale and to sponsors.

resources.title: Vice Provost policy statement on sanctions and restricted parties
World Toolkit: Embargoes, Sanctions, Prohibited Parties
OSP: Safeguards for International Research Collaboration

good_to_know: Working with entities the U.S. government lists as national security threats may affect federal funding.

title: Preparing and Routing a Grant Proposal
summary: Plan your timeline and route your proposal through your pre-award staff and the Office of Sponsored Projects (OSP) before the sponsor deadline.
key_considerations: OSP must approve every proposal before it goes to a sponsor.
OSP should receive a completed, routed record in IRES Proposal Development at least 5 business days before the sponsor deadline.
Allow the full 6 weeks if you have foreign subawards or components, or apply to CDC, HRSA, PCORI or SAMHSA.
If the sponsor deadline is after 5 PM, all OSP approvals must be done before 5 PM.
Your department or school may add its own review steps.

steps.title: Meet your pre-award administrator
steps.detail: Do this 4 to 6 weeks before the sponsor deadline.

steps.title: Finalize budget and scope
steps.detail: About 2 weeks (10 business days) out, finalize the budget, justification and scope of work, including subawards.

steps.title: Send final documents
steps.detail: Give all final documents to your pre-award administrator 7 business days before the deadline. Later files may get only a shortened review.

steps.title: OSP review and submission
steps.detail: OSP needs 5 business days for compliance checks, signature and submission. Proposal Managers submit Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM.

good_to_know: OSP generally still submits complete proposals received before the deadline, but the 5-day rule is strongly encouraged.
OSP may withdraw a submitted application before award if compliance or financial issues come up.

title: Budgeting, Including Foreign Sites
summary: Find Yale's current indirect (F&A) and fringe rates and plan extra time for budgets with foreign subawards.
key_considerations: Yale's F&A rates differ by activity and location (for example on-campus vs. off-campus research). Check the current table.
For a sponsor with no stated rate, contact an OSP Proposal or Contract Manager.
Proposals with foreign subawards or components need the full 6-week lead time.
Each subaward must come with the Subrecipient Information and Compliance (SIC) form at submission.
The budget should be a reasonable estimate of what the project needs.

steps.title: Look up rates
steps.detail: Use the Institutional Information page for F&A, fringe, equipment threshold and NIH salary cap.

steps.title: Start early with foreign sites
steps.detail: Meet your pre-award administrator 6 weeks ahead when a foreign partner is involved.

steps.title: Collect subrecipient forms
steps.detail: Get the SIC form from each subrecipient for submission.

steps.title: Write the justification
steps.detail: Explain each cost in the budget justification.

good_to_know: Data management and sharing costs for NIH go in the normal budget categories, not a separate line.

title: Limited Submission Opportunities
summary: When a funder caps how many applications Yale can send, apply through Yale's internal selection first.
key_considerations: You need approval from the Vice Provost for Research team (or a delegated unit) before the proposal goes to OSP.
Internal applications are usually due about 12 weeks before the sponsor deadline.
For opportunities announced by other units, tell OSP at least 14 weeks ahead to be sure of consideration.
If interest exceeds slots, an advisory panel ranks applicants and the VPR approves.

steps.title: Watch for announcements
steps.detail: Opportunities appear in the weekly Yale Funding Opportunities Newsletter, targeted emails and InfoReady.

steps.title: Submit an internal application
steps.detail: Include a title, two-page research summary, CV, biosketch and your department chair's contact.

steps.title: Wait for the decision
steps.detail: The VPR team tells you and OSP the result.

steps.title: Confirm or decline
steps.detail: Nominees must confirm. If you decline, tell OSP and the VPR team quickly so someone else can apply.

good_to_know: Humanities and social sciences researchers can write to internal.proposals@yale.edu.

title: Yale Global Health Seed Funding
summary: Find small internal awards from the Yale Institute for Global Health (YIGH) to start new global health projects.
key_considerations: YIGH faculty awards include the Global Health Spark Award, the Hecht Faculty Network Award, the Global Health Education Innovation Award and CIRA HIV pilot projects.
The Spark Award gives up to $10,000.
Spark applicants need a current Yale faculty appointment and YIGH faculty affiliate status.
Spending Spark funds on faculty salary is strongly discouraged.
One Spark application per person per review cycle; unfunded applicants may resubmit.

steps.title: Become a YIGH affiliate
steps.detail: Contact Mike Skonieczny to learn about affiliation.

steps.title: Pick an award
steps.detail: Review the YIGH funding and awards pages for the right fit.

steps.title: Ask about applying
steps.detail: For Spark application details, contact Kristina Talbert-Slagle (kristina.talbert-slagle@yale.edu).

steps.title: Write for a general reader
steps.detail: Spark reviewers look at innovation, feasibility, sustainability and clarity to non-experts.

good_to_know: A non-US focus is not required for the Spark Award.

title: Writing Facilities and Other Resources
summary: Describe the space, equipment and services your project can use, starting from Yale templates where they exist.
key_considerations: This section describes equipment and other resources available to the project.
Examples include lab and office space, library resources, animal facilities and computer services.
OSP's training grant page offers an 'Institutional Facilities/Yale Overview' Word template.
That template dates from 2012 and should be tailored to your application.

steps.title: Check the sponsor's instructions
steps.detail: Confirm what the funder wants in this section.

steps.title: Start from the Yale overview
steps.detail: Download the Institutional Facilities/Yale Overview template.

steps.title: Add project-specific resources
steps.detail: List the labs, cores, computing and library services you will actually use.

steps.title: Review with pre-award staff
steps.detail: Ask your pre-award administrator to check it before routing.

Research Data Lifecycle

title: IRB Approval for Research at International Sites
summary: What ethics approvals you need before doing human participant research outside the U.S.
key_considerations: Research abroad needs approval from both the Yale IRB and a local IRB or ethics board in the host country.
No recruitment, interviews or other participant contact can start until approvals are in place.
Approvals can take several months, so submit early.
List foreign collaborators and the country on the Yale protocol, and provide the local ethics approval.
If the country has no IRB, the Yale IRB will likely accept sign-off from a local NGO or official body; HRPP can help.
Using an external IRB instead of Yale's needs prior HRPP authorization.

steps.title: Identify the local ethics body
steps.detail: Find the IRB or ethics committee that covers your study site, and learn the host country's research laws.

steps.title: Submit to Yale IRB
steps.detail: Name the country and foreign collaborators in your Yale protocol.

steps.title: Get local approval
steps.detail: Obtain and send the local ethics approval to the Yale IRB.

steps.title: Ask about reliance if needed
steps.detail: If another IRB should be the reviewing board, request HRPP approval to cede review.

resources.title: Yale Ceding Review to an External IRB

good_to_know: Ask the local ethics board about local privacy rules.
Avoid having a translator who is also a participant, and generally avoid family members as translators.
If coded samples from abroad might be re-identified, resubmit to the IRB first.
important: Doing human participant research without IRB approval is a serious violation.

title: Export Controls: Travel, Shipping and Sanctioned Countries
summary: When taking laptops, equipment or data abroad, or working with sanctioned countries, needs an export control review.
key_considerations: Sending data, software or equipment abroad can be an export, whether you carry it, mail it or email it.
Laptops and phones with encryption software may need a license in some cases.
Countries under comprehensive U.S. sanctions (such as Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Syria) restrict travel, payments and data transfer.
GPS devices generally need a license for embargoed countries.
Sanctions lists change often; check with the Export Controls Office before you go.

steps.title: List what you are taking or sending
steps.detail: Include devices, software, equipment and data.

steps.title: Read the travel device guidance
steps.detail: Check Yale's guidance on electronic devices and international travel.

steps.title: Check the destination
steps.detail: See if the country is under sanctions or embargo.

steps.title: Ask for a review
steps.detail: Email the Export Controls Office before travel or shipping to a sanctioned country or when unsure.

resources.title: Export Controls and Electronic Devices in International Travel

good_to_know: Vehicles bought for a project abroad need any required OFAC licenses before purchase.
Payments to people in embargoed countries may be restricted or prohibited.

title: Research Security and Foreign Engagement
summary: What to disclose and whom to contact when your work involves foreign collaborators, funding or appointments.
key_considerations: Contact RISO before any collaboration, even informal, with people affiliated with a Country of Concern or embargoed country.
Countries of Concern include China, North Korea, Russia and Iran; embargoed places include Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Russia and Russian-occupied regions. Lists can change.
Disclose foreign funding, appointments and affiliations to Yale and to federal sponsors; accuracy is your responsibility.
Yale prohibits taking part in malign foreign talent recruitment programs and requires disclosure of involvement.
Senior/key personnel need research security training before submitting Other Support.

steps.title: Check the countries involved
steps.detail: See whether partners are tied to a Country of Concern or embargoed country.

steps.title: Contact RISO early
steps.detail: Email RISO before the collaboration starts so they can assess risk.

steps.title: Disclose to Yale
steps.detail: Report outside activities and interests in Yale's disclosure system.

steps.title: Disclose to sponsors
steps.detail: List foreign support, appointments and visitors as Other Support where required.

good_to_know: Working with entities the U.S. lists as national security threats may affect federal funding or require mitigation.
important: Email research.security@yale.edu before collaborating with anyone tied to a Country of Concern or embargoed country.

title: Disclosing Conflicts of Interest
summary: Who must file a conflict of interest disclosure at Yale, when, and how.
key_considerations: Faculty, staff and anyone responsible for designing, conducting or reporting a sponsored project must disclose, even if they have nothing to report.
Disclose at least once a year, and within 30 days of a new significant financial interest.
Disclosures must be current before award funds are spent.
PHS/NIH and DOE investigators must disclose travel paid for by foreign universities or governments.

steps.title: Open the disclosure form
steps.detail: Complete the External Interest Disclosure Form in the COI portal using your NetID.

steps.title: Report travel if required
steps.detail: PHS/NIH and DOE investigators file a Travel Disclosure Form.

steps.title: Keep it current
steps.detail: Update within 30 days of any new significant financial interest and renew yearly.

steps.title: Follow any management plan
steps.detail: If a conflict is found, the COI Office will work with you on how to manage it.

resources.title: COI Office FAQ
resources.note: Who, when and how to disclose

good_to_know: Technical help: COI Call Center, (203) 737-5954, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Your disclosure status shows in Workday Learning.

title: Protecting Research Data Across Borders
summary: How to classify your data, handle EU/EEA personal data under GDPR, and set up data use agreements.
key_considerations: Yale data is High, Moderate or Low risk; human subject and patient information is High Risk.
If any part of a dataset is High Risk, treat the whole dataset as High Risk.
Store data only in Yale systems approved for its risk level.
Personal data collected in or transferred from the EEA is subject to GDPR, and you need a lawful basis to process it.
Data Use Agreements need a written contract signed by Yale, whatever their value; non-profit suppliers go to OSP, for-profit to Procurement.
HIPAA may apply if identifiable participant data comes back to Yale; consider de-identifying first.

steps.title: Classify your data
steps.detail: Use the Data Classification Questionnaire to find your data's risk level.

steps.title: Pick approved storage
steps.detail: Choose a Yale service rated for that risk level.

steps.title: Check GDPR
steps.detail: If data comes from people in the EEA, read Yale's GDPR research guidance and talk to HRPP.

steps.title: Set up a Data Use Agreement
steps.detail: Route DUAs through OSP or Procurement before receiving or sharing data.

good_to_know: Yale offers a CITI course called GDPR for Research and Higher Ed.
Health, genetic, racial or ethnic data are sensitive under GDPR and need extra protection.

title: Registering Suppliers in the Yale Supplier Gateway
summary: Get a new supplier, including a foreign one, set up in Yale's Supplier Gateway so you can pay them.
key_considerations: A supplier must be Active in Supplier Gateway before Yale can pay them.
Check the Buying Guide first: preferred suppliers are already set up with negotiated pricing.
All supplier changes are made in Supplier Gateway by the supplier or a proxy user.
Yale students are best set up through the Prizes and Awards (PandA) process.

steps.title: Check for an existing or preferred supplier
steps.detail: Search the Buying Guide and Supplier Gateway so you do not create a duplicate record.

steps.title: Pick the disbursement type
steps.detail: Use the Disbursement Type Selection Chart to choose how the payee will be paid.

steps.title: Invite the supplier
steps.detail: Send a Supplier Invite through Supplier Gateway. The supplier registers and uploads tax and bank details.

steps.title: Confirm the supplier is Active
steps.detail: Check the status before you request payment. Contact the Financial Support Center if you get stuck.

resources.title: Supplier Set Up and Change Requests
Payments to Non-US Individuals and Entities

good_to_know: Paying a foreign supplier also triggers tax rules; use the International Payment Planning tools each time.

title: Buying Goods and Services for Work Abroad
summary: Choose the right Yale purchasing method and follow quote rules when buying for a global project.
key_considerations: Workday purchase requisitions are the preferred method and should be created before work starts.
The Purchasing Card covers travel, business goods and limited services within set limits; it normally cannot withdraw cash at ATMs.
Under $10,000, no competing quotes are needed if the price is reasonable.
From $10,000 to $250,000 with a non-preferred supplier, get quotes, a bid, or a sole source justification.
Over $250,000 on federal funds needs an independent cost estimate, competition or sole source justification, and a price or cost analysis.

steps.title: Use a preferred supplier if you can
steps.detail: Preferred suppliers are already competitively bid, so extra bidding is usually not needed.

steps.title: Make sure the supplier is set up
steps.detail: New suppliers must be registered and Active in Supplier Gateway.

steps.title: Create a requisition in Workday
steps.detail: A purchase order is generated when the requisition is approved.

steps.title: Pay foreign vendors correctly
steps.detail: Check the International Payment Planning tools and contact the International Tax Office before paying.

resources.title: Supplier Set Up and Change Requests

good_to_know: Yale does not reimburse purchases made on personal Amazon accounts.
Policy exceptions go to the Controller's Office (controllers.office@yale.edu).

title: Issuing Subawards to Foreign Partners
summary: Send part of a sponsored award to a partner institution abroad through the Office of Sponsored Projects.
key_considerations: First decide if the partner is a subrecipient or a vendor using OSP's checklist.
Foreign subawards may need prior sponsor approval; ask your OSP Award/Contract Manager.
For a foreign subrecipient, OSP decides whether export control review is needed.
OSP usually will not issue the subaward until protocol approvals and the partner's PHS conflict-of-interest certification are in place.
OSP assesses the partner's finances and internal controls before issuing.

steps.title: Confirm subrecipient status
steps.detail: Use the Subrecipient vs. Vendor Checklist.

steps.title: Check sponsor approval
steps.detail: Ask your OSP Award/Contract Manager whether the sponsor must approve a foreign subaward.

steps.title: Gather documents
steps.detail: Your business office collects the SIC form, scope of work, budget and justification. New partners also need audit or financial statements and a new Workday supplier request.

steps.title: Send to your GCAT mailbox
steps.detail: Include the Yale PI name, IRES record number and Notice of Award number.

steps.title: OSP drafts and executes
steps.detail: The Subaward Manager drafts the agreement, both sides sign, and it is set up in Workday.

resources.title: Supplier Set Up and Change Requests

good_to_know: Talk to OSP early; sponsor approval and compliance checks take time.
important: Foreign subawards can raise export control and research security questions; check with OSP before committing to a partner.

title: Hiring and Paying People Abroad
summary: Find a compliant way to staff or pay people outside the U.S. for your Yale project.
key_considerations: In most situations Yale cannot directly employ people outside the U.S.
Options include a host-country partner, a Professional Employment Organization, an independent contractor, or a local Yale entity.
Consultants abroad must be properly classified as consultants, not employees; ask the Tax Department if unsure.
Use the International Payment Planning tool every time you pay a non-U.S. person or entity.
Staffing solutions can take weeks or months.

steps.title: Contact the IOCC early
steps.detail: Describe the role and location. The IOCC reviews labor, tax, immigration and budget issues.

steps.title: Submit the right questionnaire
steps.detail: Faculty and trainees send questionnaires to iocc@yale.edu; staff go to Employee Services (YSM staff to their HR Partner).

steps.title: Plan the payment
steps.detail: Run the International Payment Planning tool for individuals or entities.

steps.title: Set up the payee
steps.detail: Register the person or entity as a supplier in Supplier Gateway before payment.

resources.title: Payments to Non-US Individuals and Entities

good_to_know: International tax questions: internationaltax@yale.edu.
Employment questions for staff: employee.services@yale.edu.

title: Shipping Equipment, Supplies and Specimens Abroad
summary: Ship research materials and other items internationally through Yale's required system with the right reviews.
key_considerations: Shipments Yale is responsible for must go through eShipGlobal unless an exception is granted.
Only lab and non-administrative clinical staff may ship research or clinical materials.
Everyone who ships or receives research materials must complete required training.
Some microorganisms, toxins and their genetic elements are export controlled.
Shipments flagged for review in eShipGlobal go to EHS for approval.

steps.title: Complete shipping training
steps.detail: Take the courses required for your material, such as Category A or B biological shipping.

steps.title: Check export controls
steps.detail: Review the export-controlled organisms and toxins list. Ask EHS for help before you ship.

steps.title: Prepare a commercial invoice
steps.detail: Include addresses, item description, quantity, value and reason for shipping.

steps.title: Create the shipment in eShipGlobal
steps.detail: The system flags import or export rules and routes some shipments to EHS.

good_to_know: Non-research export questions go to the Office of Export Controls at exports@yale.edu.
EHS main line: 203-785-3550.
important: Shipping export-controlled materials without review can break U.S. law; check with EHS first.

title: Traveling Abroad for Yale Work
summary: Register your trip and use Yale's International SOS assistance to stay safe while traveling.

office.name: Enterprise Risk Management (Office of the General Counsel)

key_considerations: Register travel in the Yale Travel Registry so Yale can reach you in an emergency.
Students and current employees are automatically enrolled in International SOS at no cost.
ISOS is assistance, not insurance: no trip cancellation or baggage coverage.
Yale business travel includes out-of-country medical coverage up to $250,000 for trips up to 365 days.
Higher-risk destinations can get a custom ISOS pre-departure briefing.

steps.title: Register your trip
steps.detail: Follow the Yale Travel Registry instructions before you leave.

steps.title: Get the ISOS card and app
steps.detail: Download the ISOS ID card and assistance app.

steps.title: Learn emergency steps
steps.detail: Know what to do in an emergency abroad.

steps.title: Call ISOS if you need help
steps.detail: Use the Yale line +1 215-942-8478; you can ask to reverse charges.

good_to_know: File medical claims with AIG within 60 days and copy risk.management@yale.edu.
Coverage excludes travel to your country of citizenship and routine care.

title: Running Operations in Another Country
summary: Handle banking, cash and local setup questions when Yale work happens abroad.
key_considerations: Yale generally cannot open a bank account abroad until it registers a local branch or subsidiary.
Do not open a bank account in your own name for Yale business.
Carry only the cash you need; the Purchasing Card normally does not allow ATM withdrawals.
Carrying more than $10,000 in or out of the U.S. must be declared.
Hiring locally usually needs a registered local presence and compliant payroll.

steps.title: Talk to the IOCC early
steps.detail: They advise on local registration, staffing and compliance.

steps.title: Request a bank account if needed
steps.detail: Contact Treasury Services with the program, purpose and duration.

steps.title: Plan cash and payments
steps.detail: Follow the policy on obtaining cash abroad and use the International Payment Planning tool.

steps.title: Ask about wires
steps.detail: Contact the Financial Support Center (askfinance@yale.edu) for international wire transfers.

good_to_know: The Office of International Affairs can help with questions like setting up a research office abroad.

title: Publishing Open Access
summary: Use Yale Library agreements to publish open access at lower or no cost, and meet the NIH public access rule.
key_considerations: Yale has agreements that waive or discount article fees with publishers such as PLOS, Cambridge, Sage (hybrid only) and others.
Usually you must be the corresponding author and pick the required Creative Commons license.
Several agreements need a yale.edu or ynhh.org email address.
NIH requires author accepted manuscripts accepted on or after July 1, 2025 to go to PubMed Central on acceptance, with no embargo.
EliScholar is Yale's free, long-term repository for scholars' work.

steps.title: Check your journal
steps.detail: Look up the publisher's terms and dates in the Library guide.

steps.title: Submit as corresponding author
steps.detail: Use your Yale email where required.

steps.title: Choose the license
steps.detail: Select the required Creative Commons license at acceptance.

steps.title: Meet NIH public access
steps.detail: If NIH-funded, submit the accepted manuscript to PubMed Central.

good_to_know: Health sciences authors can contact medlibscholcomm@yale.edu.
Agreement terms change; confirm before you submit.

title: Data Management and Sharing
summary: Write an NIH data management and sharing plan and choose where to deposit your data.
key_considerations: All NIH applications need a two-page data management and sharing plan.
DMS costs go in normal budget categories and the budget justification, not a separate line.
The person managing the data is responsible for compliance; OSP does not monitor it.
Check Yale's Data Classification Guidelines before choosing a repository.
Yale Dataverse is a generalist repository for sharing research data of any type.

steps.title: Draft the plan
steps.detail: Use the NIH template or DMPTool.

steps.title: Get help
steps.detail: Ask Yale Library for a data management plan consultation.

steps.title: Budget the costs
steps.detail: Include personnel, curation, deposit fees and preservation in the justification.

steps.title: Deposit and share
steps.detail: Use a domain repository or a generalist one such as Yale Dataverse.

good_to_know: Email osphelp@yale.edu with subject 'NIH Data Mandate/DMP' for policy questions.
important: Discuss data sharing with international and industry partners early, and follow all human participant privacy rules.

title: Sharing Your Work Through YSM News
summary: Submit your research news, awards and events to Yale School of Medicine newsletters.
key_considerations: The weekly YSM News & Recognition newsletter covers YSM-led research, awards, appointments and milestones.
Events must be created in the YSM Calendar Tool to appear in the Friday events newsletter.
For press and public relations, contact the university Office of Public Affairs and Communications (OPAC).

steps.title: Submit a story
steps.detail: Use the YSM News & Recognition form.

steps.title: Share internal news
steps.detail: Use the Submit MyYSM News page.

steps.title: Ask questions
steps.detail: Email the site editor at ysm.editor@yale.edu.

resources.note: How to submit to YSM newsletters

title: Closing Out an Award
summary: Finish final reports and close subawards on time so you stay in good standing for future funding.
key_considerations: Federal closeout generally runs 90 days after the project end date; check your award terms.
NIH wants the final financial report, final progress report and final invention statement within 90 calendar days.
The PI submits the final technical report; SPFA prepares final financial reports.
For outgoing subawards, confirm each partner sent all reports and its final invoice first.
Late NSF final reports delay review of pending proposals for the PI and co-PIs.

steps.title: Plan with your business office
steps.detail: Work with your Department Business Office on reconciliations and account closeout.

steps.title: Collect partner deliverables
steps.detail: Get final reports and the final invoice from each subrecipient.

steps.title: Submit final reports
steps.detail: Send the final technical or progress report; your OSP Award or Contract Manager can help.

steps.title: Report inventions
steps.detail: Yale Ventures works with OSP to confirm any final inventions.

good_to_know: Closeout does not end record retention or financial accountability duties.
